table_row: A direct-edge cycle is supplied | Report an invalid strict-order input through validation; transitivity alone does not reject it
narrative: OWL transitivity is an entailment rule, not an integrity constraint: declaring precedes transitive does not by itself make a reasoner reject a cyclic input. A direct-edge cycle among A, B, C is a strict-order violation (it would require e_A < e_A after closure) and must be caught by an explicit validation step before any adjacency or precedence query runs, not left to the ontology to reject implicitly.

illustrative_expectation.basis: the direct-edge graph contains a cycle A -> B -> C -> A, which is inconsistent with any strict total or partial order over occurrence intervals
illustrative_expectation.note: this must be caught by a validation pass distinct from ontology consistency checking; declaring precedes owl:TransitiveProperty does not entail rejection of this input on its own

unresolved_before_adoption: where this validation pass would live relative to the existing PRO/SOLID validation and semantic-consistency gates
